resources.string: PS2 memory cards (Mcd001.ps2, Mcd002.ps2). Each card holds the saves of many games, so the cards are only synced once you turn on Shared memory cards for this folder.

GameCube memory cards (MemoryCardA.USA.raw and the like). Each card holds the saves of many games, so the cards are only synced once you turn on Shared memory cards for this folder. Not synced: GCI folders (GC/USA/Card A, one file per save; their names do not tell which game file they belong to) and Wii saves (kept in Dolphin\'s Wii folder). Dolphin writes a card file when GameCube slot A is set to a memory card instead of a GCI folder.

RomM keeps every save with a game. Search for the game to keep this folder\'s PS2 memory cards with; any PlayStation 2 game on your RomM will do. Choose the same game on every handheld. When a card changed on both sides, you choose which one stays.

RomM keeps every save with a game. Search for the game to keep this folder\'s GameCube memory cards with; any GameCube game on your RomM will do. Choose the same game on every handheld. When a card changed on both sides, you choose which one stays.

No: a hand-off moves the saves of one game, and %1$s keeps the saves of all its games together on its memory cards. Save sync can keep a whole card with RomM instead: in Settings → Save sync, add its folder (usually %2$s) and turn on Shared memory cards, with the same RomM game on both handhelds. When a card changed on both sides, you choose which one stays.
